items.from: Inaugural members of the Anthropic National Security and Public Sector Advisory Council (11 named in fact)
items.fact: Anthropic launched the council on 2025-08-27 with 11 inaugural members: Roy Blunt, David S. Cohen, Richard Fontaine, Christopher Fonzone, Lisa E. Gordon-Hagerty, Josh Hodges, Jill M. Hruby, Mike Kuiken, Dave Luber, Patrick M. Shanahan and Jon Tester. Anthropic said it would announce more members in the coming months.
items.quote: Today, we are honored to welcome the following inaugural members
items.missing: Current membership after the inaugural list; the start date of each member's seat on the council.
items.notes: Former federal roles per the same page: Blunt, former US Senator (Missouri); Cohen, former CIA Deputy Director and Treasury Under Secretary for Terrorism and Financial Intelligence; Fontaine, Long-Term Benefit Trust member (see T1.10); Fonzone, former ODNI General Counsel under Biden and NSC Legal Adviser; Gordon-Hagerty, former NNSA Administrator in the first Trump administration; Hodges, former NSC Senior Director for Western Hemisphere Affairs in the first Trump administration; Hruby, former NNSA Administrator under Biden; Kuiken, former national security adviser to Senate Majority Leader Schumer; Luber, former NSA Director of Cybersecurity and Cyber Command executive director; Shanahan, former Acting and Deputy Secretary of Defense in the first Trump administration; Tester, former US Senator (Montana). Coverage note: 14 searches found no Commerce or BIS hire; the only Office of Science and Technology Policy hire found is Sihao Huang (T1.14), whose administration is not stated.

items.capacity: Head of National Security (head of national security policy)
items.fact: An Aspen Security Forum speaker bio, undated, says Tarun Chhabra is head of national security policy at Anthropic. Before that he coordinated US technology-competition and ally technology strategy as NSC Deputy Assistant to the President and Coordinator for Technology and National Security, from 2021 to 2025 per the same bio.
items.quote: Tarun Chhabra is head of national security policy at Anthropic.
items.missing: Anthropic start date. The Senate Foreign Relations statement for the record (file name suggests 2025-12-02, https://www.foreign.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/5c78c941-bd21-2468-1d2c-957537481348/120225_Chhabra_Testimony.pdf) reportedly lists him as Head of National Security, Anthropic, but the PDF was not readable by page.py, so that is not verified here.
items.notes: Earlier NSC titles: Special Assistant to the President and Senior Director for Technology and National Security (Wikipedia entry, secondary). A reported article (undated in my read, Yahoo syndication of a Daily Beast piece) says Anthropic recently hired him. Earlier white house service 2021-2025 per Aspen bio.

items.fact: Elizabeth Kelly is Head of Beneficial Deployments at Anthropic, per her own Fortune byline dated 2025-12-02. She was founding Director of the US AI Safety Institute at the Department of Commerce before that.
items.quote: Elizabeth Kelly, Head of Beneficial Deployments at Anthropic.
items.missing: Anthropic's own announcement of the appointment and a verified start date. The 2025-03 start comes only from an undated Daily Beast piece (Yahoo syndication) saying she joined in March after two years in the White House; the year is inferred from context.
items.notes: Earlier roles: founding Director, US AISI (Commerce); Special Assistant to the President for Economic Policy at the White House National Economic Council (Concordia speaker page, third party, line truncated; dates not given). Departure from AISI reported February 2025 in search results (not read).

items.capacity: Head of Geopolitics and Security (2023 record); Head of Global Affairs (CNAS profile, undated)
items.fact: A Singapore Conference on AI profile dated 2023-12-04 lists Michael Sellitto as Head of Geopolitics and Security at Anthropic, the earliest dated Anthropic record found. A CNAS profile, undated, lists him as Head of Global Affairs at Anthropic.
items.quote: Head of Geopolitics and Security, Anthropic
items.missing: Anthropic start date. Current title: a 2026-08-04 report names Mariano-Florentino Cuellar Anthropic's first chief global affairs officer (T1.15), which may conflict with the CNAS title for Sellitto.
items.notes: Earlier federal role per CNAS profile (https://cnas.org/people/michael-sellitto, read): Director for Cybersecurity Policy on the National Security Council staff from 2015-2018. Before Anthropic he was founding deputy director of Stanford HAI (CNAS profile).

items.fact: A reported article with no date in my read (Yahoo syndication of a Daily Beast piece) says Ben Buchanan, Biden's special adviser on AI, is an adviser to a $60 billion Silicon Valley company, in a passage about Anthropic; the company is not named in that sentence. No Anthropic page, council listing or second source confirmed it in my searches.
items.quote: is an adviser to the $60 billion Silicon Valley company
items.missing: Confirmation of the company from Anthropic or a second outlet; start date; title; whether the role is current. Low confidence: one reported source.
items.notes: Not on the 11-name council list (T1.1). Earlier White House role: Special Adviser for AI, per a Johns Hopkins SAIS faculty page and an author bio giving 2021 to 2025 (search snippets, pages not read). A Washington Examiner article (2026-04-17) links Buchanan and a colleague to CSET, a nonprofit funded by an Anthropic investor; that is a funding tie, not an Anthropic role.

items.capacity: Former employee (title and dates not stated)
items.fact: A 2025 Warsaw Security Forum speaker profile says Christopher Kirchhoff 'previously worked for Anthropic' and lists his current role as head of applied AI strategy and global security at Scale AI. The profile gives no Anthropic dates or title.
items.missing: Anthropic start and end dates, title and an Anthropic-side record. This profile is the only source read for the Anthropic link, and my searches found no Anthropic announcement. Not on the council list.
items.notes: Earlier government service per the same profile: National Security Council Director for Strategic Planning, senior civilian aide to the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and adviser to the Counselor to the President in the White House Chief of Staff's office, across three administrations (no years given). Founding Partner, Defense Innovation Unit (2016-2017), per the profile header. A search snippet attributed the NSC post to the Obama administration; not separately verified.

items.fact: page not read: a search result (Axios headline) reports that Dean Ball is heading to OpenAI, and none of my results reported an Anthropic role for him.
items.quote: AI scholar Dean Ball says he's heading to OpenAI
items.missing: Any source placing him at Anthropic. A reader who sees an Anthropic claim should check Anthropic's own pages first.
items.notes: Source date taken from the URL. A Foundation for American Innovation post (search snippet, not read) says he starts at OpenAI as Head of Strategic Futures on July 6. Earlier White House role: advising on emerging technology, per The Free Press (search summary only, not read).

items.fact: Anthropic announced on 2026-02-13 that Chris Liddell had been appointed to its board of directors. He is a former CFO of Microsoft, General Motors and International Paper, and was Deputy White House Chief of Staff in President Trump's first term.
items.quote: Chris Liddell has been appointed to Anthropic’s Board of Directors.
items.missing: Committee assignments (press coverage says none were specified); the years of his White House role, which the announcement does not give.
items.notes: Earlier federal: Deputy White House Chief of Staff during President Trump's first term (Anthropic page, dates not given there). Coverage ties the timing to IPO preparation (reported, not read).

items.fact: Anthropic announced on 2026-07-09 that its Long-Term Benefit Trust had appointed Ben Bernanke, a Brookings Distinguished Fellow and former Chair of the Federal Reserve, as its newest member.
items.quote: former Chair of the Federal Reserve
items.missing: Effective date (the page gives only the publication date); whether he holds any current federal office (not stated).
items.notes: Earlier federal: Chair of the Federal Reserve, 2006 to 2014 (same page: 'Bernanke led the Federal Reserve from 2006 to 2014'). Counting a Fed chair as a federal official is my judgment; the page does not say so.

items.fact: TechCrunch reported on 2025-06-06 that Anthropic had appointed Richard Fontaine, CEO of the Center for a New American Security, to its long-term benefit trust. The Anthropic council page also lists him as an LTBT member.
items.quote: appointed a national security expert, Richard Fontaine, to its long-term benefit trust
items.missing: Federal status: the council page describes him as a former foreign policy adviser to the late Senator John McCain (a Senate staff role, dates not given). Not clearly a federal official. End date.
items.notes: Also on the inaugural council list (T1.1), where Anthropic states he is a Long-Term Benefit Trust member.

items.fact: Defense One reported on 2026-05-01 that James Baker, who led the Defense Department's Office of Net Assessment, is joining Anthropic as a strategist-in-residence. The report gives no start date.
items.missing: Start date; whether the role is employment or a contract; an Anthropic announcement (not found).
items.notes: Earlier federal: led the Defense Department's Office of Net Assessment from 2015 to 2025, per the same report ('led the Defense Department's Office of Net Assessment'), which says the office was temporarily closed by the Trump administration. A Washington Technology version of the same story exists (https://washingtontechnology.com/companies/2026/05/former-head-pentagons-think-tank-joins-anthropic/413311/, not read).

items.capacity: National security policy lead (one unsourced search summary; unconfirmed)
items.fact: page not read: one search summary said Sasha Baker leads Anthropic's national security policy team and earlier served as a Biden-era deputy under secretary of defense for policy. A follow-up search returned no Anthropic page or report naming her and only James Baker (T1.11), so the name may be a conflation.
items.missing: Any source naming Sasha Baker at Anthropic. The claim came from a search summary with no checkable URL.
items.notes: Not confirmed by any page read. Compare T1.11 (James Baker, Office of Net Assessment), which is confirmed by a read source.

items.fact: A reported article, undated in my read (Yahoo syndication of a Daily Beast piece), calls Benjamin Merkel Anthropic's legislative analyst. It says he was Biden's Special Assistant to the President and Senate Liaison from January 2024 to January 2025.
items.quote: Benjamin Merkel was Biden's Special Assistant to the President and Senate Liaison
items.missing: Anthropic start date; a primary Anthropic or White House source; article date.
items.notes: Earlier federal: Special Assistant to the President and Senate Liaison, January 2024 to January 2025 (same article). Not on the council list.

items.capacity: Compute strategy head (per report headline; exact title not confirmed)
items.fact: Phemex News reported on 2026-09-16 that Sihao Huang, a former senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence and emerging technologies at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, has joined Anthropic.
items.quote: Sihao Huang Joins Anthropic as Compute Strategy Head
items.missing: A primary Anthropic announcement or White House source; exact start date (2026-09 is the article month, not a verified start); OSTP role dates and administration, which the report does not state.
items.notes: Low confidence: a crypto news aggregator is the only source read for this. Earlier federal: Senior Policy Advisor for Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (same report, dates not given).

items.capacity: First chief global affairs officer (oversees policy and government relations; reports to Daniela Amodei)
items.fact: The Next Web reported on 2026-08-04 that Anthropic named Tino Cuellar its first chief global affairs officer to manage government ties. The Harvard Crimson reported the same appointment, with him reporting to Daniela Amodei.
items.quote: Anthropic named Tino Cuellar its first chief global affairs officer
items.missing: Federal-service record: the pages read describe him as a former California Supreme Court justice and a Carnegie Endowment leader, not as a federal official. One search snippet (not read) links him to a Biden-era intelligence advisory board. Exact start date (2026-08-04 is the announcement date).
items.notes: Included because the Anthropic role is documented; drop from a federal-only list if the reader's scope excludes non-federal service. Also a Harvard Corporation member and on leave from Stanford Law (Harvard Crimson, https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2026/8/4/cuellar-anthropic-global-affairs/, read). Title overlap with Michael Sellitto (T1.4) is unresolved.
